chief_complaint: heavy periods, fatigue, and craving ice
hpi_details: 28F presents with extreme fatigue for 6 months. She reports very heavy menstrual periods, changing a pad every 2 hours for 7 days each month. She also reports a strange craving to chew on ice cubes.
concerns: worried about losing too much blood

core_concepts: Most common cause of anemia worldwide, often due to blood loss (menorrhagia in young women, GI bleed in older adults) or poor diet.
Pica (craving ice/pagophagia) is a highly specific symptom.
common_misconceptions: Treating the anemia without addressing the underlying cause (menorrhagia).
dangerous_errors: Assuming iron deficiency in an older adult or postmenopausal woman is dietary (must rule out colon cancer).
management_principles: Oral iron supplementation with vitamin C, gynecology referral for menorrhagia.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: UpToDate & National Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines 2026

reference_soap.subjective: 28F with fatigue, pagophagia, and heavy menstrual bleeding.
reference_soap.objective: Pale conjunctiva, tachycardia (HR 105). No spooning of nails.
reference_soap.assessment: Iron deficiency anemia secondary to menorrhagia and possibly vegan diet.
reference_soap.plan: CBC, iron panel, ferritin. Start oral ferrous sulfate. OB/GYN referral.

learning_objectives: Recognize pagophagia and menorrhagia as classic clues for iron deficiency anemia.

teaching.one_liner: Fatigue and pagophagia (ice craving) in a young female with heavy menstrual bleeding and a vegan diet.
red_flags: Occult GI bleeding (not typically in this age group)

must_ask.say: How heavy are your periods, and how many pads do you soak through in a day?
Have you had any unusual cravings, like craving ice, dirt, or starch?
Have you noticed any blood in your stool, or black tarry stools?
Can you tell me about your typical diet, especially how much meat or iron-rich food you eat?
How is the fatigue affecting your day-to-day activities?

history.answer: I have been feeling completely exhausted for the past several months, and my periods have become unusually heavy.
It is an overwhelming lack of energy and physical weakness all over, rather than just feeling drowsy or sleepy.
It crept up on me gradually about six months ago, and it has been getting steadily worse without any specific event triggering it.
I struggle to get through my regular workday, and resting over the weekend does not restore my energy at all.
I feel drained and sluggish all day long, from the minute I wake up until I go to sleep.
I sleep about seven to eight hours every night without waking up, and my roommate has never heard me snore or gasp for air.
I feel frustrated and down about having no energy, but I do not have depression and have never had thoughts of hurting myself.
I get lightheaded when I stand up quickly and breathless climbing stairs, but I have not had black tarry stools or blood in my bowel movements.
My bleeding lasts for seven full days every month, and I have to change a soaked pad every two hours day and night.
Yes, over the past few months I have developed this intense craving to constantly chew on ice cubes throughout the day.
No, I have not noticed unusual bruising on my skin, and my gums do not bleed when I brush my teeth.
No, I do not have any tingling, numbness, or pins-and-needles sensations in my hands or feet.
I tend to feel chilly more easily lately, but I have not had unexplained weight gain, constipation, or dry skin.
No, I am not excessively thirsty, and I am not running to the bathroom to pee more than usual.
No, my skin has not darkened or turned bronzed, and my appetite has been normal.
No, I have no skin itching, strange tastes in my mouth, or changes in how much urine I make.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss.
I get winded when walking uphill or up the stairs, but my legs have not swollen and I do not have chest pain.
I switched to a strict vegan diet about one year ago, and I have not been taking any iron pills or multivitamins.
My office work can get busy, but my stress level is manageable, and I only drink one cup of coffee a day.
I assumed I was just burned out and stressed from work, which is why I waited this long to see a doctor.
I am worried that losing so much blood during my heavy periods every month is draining my body and making me sick.
I was hoping we could do some blood tests today to check my blood count and find out why I have no energy.
I have always been healthy and have never been diagnosed with any medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never stayed overnight in a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, or dietary supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or environmental triggers.
I have never smoked cigarettes, vaped, or used any tobacco products.
I rarely drink, maybe just a single glass of wine once or twice a month on social occasions.
I work as an accountant in an office and live in an apartment with a roommate.
Both of my parents are alive and healthy, and there is no family history of anemia, bleeding disorders, or thyroid disease.
My last period started two weeks ago, and my cycle is regular, arriving every twenty-eight days.
I am sexually active with one partner, we consistently use condoms, and there is no chance that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, heart rate is 105 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.7°C, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Marked conjunctival pallor is present bilaterally; sclerae are white and anicteric.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and moves smoothly with swallowing without palpable nodules.
No palpable cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Regular tachycardic rhythm with normal S1 and S2; faint systolic ejection flow murmur audible at the left sternal border without gallop or rub.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with vesicular breath sounds and no crackles or wheezes.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender without hepatomegaly or splenomegaly.
Skin is pale without rashes or petechiae, and fingernails show no koilonychia or spooning.
No pitting edema in either lower extremity.
